- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price movements; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days of horizon.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.00), model tends to lag behind true price; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early period (first 10 days) and underestimate late period (last 10 days); adjust early days down 0.5–1.5% and late days up 0.5–1.5%.
